binding_rules.summary: Article2(1)(b) includes Union-established deployers; Article2 exclusions must be assessed against actual professional use.

citations.quote: (b)  | deployers of AI systems that have their place of establishment or are located within the Union;

binding_rules.summary: Provider requires development/commissioning and market/service under own name; an inventory label alone is insufficient. Deployer is use under own authority except personal non-professional use.

citations.quote: (3)  | ‘provider’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body that develops an AI system or a general-purpose AI model or that has an AI system or a general-purpose AI model developed and places it on the market or puts the AI system into service under its own name or trademark, whether for payment or free of charge;

deployer_citation.quote: (4)  | ‘deployer’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body using an AI system under its authority except where the AI system is used in the course of a personal non-professional activity;

binding_rules.summary: Provider duty for direct AI interaction; context-dependent obviousness exception is not assumed from an avatar graphic. Criminal-use exception does not match reported professional education uses.

citations.quote: 1.   Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect, taking into account the circumstances and the context of use.

binding_rules.condition: AI intended to interact directly with natural persons
exceptions: obvious to reasonably well-informed observant circumspect person in context

binding_rules.summary: Provider duty for machine-readable detectable synthetic outputs; technical feasibility matters. Standard editing/no substantial alteration exception is conditional, not inferred from a visible label.

citations.quote: 2.   Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.

exceptions: standard editing or no substantial alteration of input/semantics

binding_rules.summary: Deployer notice duty for emotion recognition or biometric categorisation requires actual biometric/emotion/category facts; human adjudication does not settle applicability.

citations.quote: 3.   Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system, and shall process the personal data in accordance with Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680, as applicable.

binding_rules.summary: Deepfake requires resemblance to existing persons/objects/places/entities/events and false apparent authenticity or truthfulness. Synthetic media is not automatically a deepfake.

citations.quote: (60)  | ‘deep fake’ means AI-generated or manipulated image, audio or video content that resembles existing persons, objects, places, entities or events and would falsely appear to a person to be authentic or truthful;

binding_rules.summary: Deployer must disclose generated/manipulated deepfake media. Evidently artistic/creative/satirical/fictional work receives an adapted manner of disclosure, not blanket approval.

citations.quote: 4.   Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated. This obligation shall not apply where the use is authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offence.

adapted_disclosure.quote: Where the content forms part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous work or programme, the transparency obligations set out in this paragraph are limited to disclosure of the existence of such generated or manipulated content in an appropriate manner that does not hamper the display or enjoyment of the work.

binding_rules.summary: Deployer disclosure duty applies to generated/manipulated text published to inform public on public-interest matters. Human/editorial review exception also requires editorial responsibility; individual administrative replies differ from public-interest publication.

citations.quote: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest shall disclose that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated.

editorial_exception.quote: This obligation shall not apply where the use is authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences or where the AI-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control and where a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for the publication of the content.

binding_rules.summary: Applicable information must be clear/distinguishable and accessible by first interaction or exposure; visible-label report alone does not establish format/accessibility.

citations.quote: 5.   The information referred to in paragraphs 1 to 4 shall be provided to the natural persons concerned in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure. The information shall conform to the applicable accessibility requirements.

binding_rules.summary: Article50 does not extinguish ChapterIII or other national/Union transparency requirements. This draft does not decide all AI Act duties.

citations.quote: 6.   Paragraphs 1 to 4 shall not affect the requirements and obligations set out in Chapter III, and shall be without prejudice to other transparency obligations laid down in Union or national law for deployers of AI systems.

binding_rules.summary: July amendment replaces Article50(7) code-assessment mechanism; original wording retained as predecessor, not treated as current approval.

citations.quote: (20)  | in Article 50, paragraph 7 is replaced by the following: ‘7.   The Commission shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level to facilitate the effective implementation of the obligations regarding the detection, marking and labelling of artificially generated or manipulated content.
